# awesome-japanese-speech

A curated list of **Japanese speech recognition (ASR), speech synthesis (TTS) and LLMs**, plus the models around spoken dialogue (voice activity detection, turn-taking, backchannels).

[日本語](README.md)

- Focused on models you can run locally, with **Japanese support, streaming, license (commercial use) and runtime** side by side.
- Some models have **numbers measured on the same machine under the same conditions** (character error rate, latency, RTF) together with the scripts, in [benchmarks/](benchmarks/).
- Written with spoken dialogue systems in mind, so **latency matters as much as accuracy**.

> Always check the official license of each model. "TBD" means we have not verified it yet.
> The "Commercial" column is a hint, not legal advice.

"Streaming: yes" means text appears while the user is still speaking; "pseudo" means short chunks are re-recognized each time.

## TTS

"Streaming: yes" means audio can start before the whole sentence is synthesized.

| Model | Developer | Japanese | Streaming | Runtime | Size | License | Commercial | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [AivisSpeech](https://github.com/Aivis-Project/AivisSpeech-Engine) | Aivis Project | dedicated | — | standalone engine + HTTP API (no Python) | per AIVMX model | engine LGPL-3.0 / voices per model | per voice/model | Best overall: fast (long-text RTF 0.054), stable reading, easy setup ([results](benchmarks/tts/2026-08-19.md)) |
| [VOICEVOX](https://github.com/VOICEVOX/voicevox_engine) | VOICEVOX | dedicated | — | standalone engine + HTTP API, voicevox_core (C API / Python) | — | engine LGPL-3.0 / per-character terms for voices | per voice/model | The standard Japanese TTS; terms differ per character. Not measured |
| [Irodori-TTS v4.1 Small](https://github.com/Aratako/Irodori-TTS) | Aratako | dedicated | — | PyTorch | ~2.9 GB (runtime VRAM 3.6 GB) | MIT (code and model) | yes | Best quality and features: voice design by caption and cloning; long-text RTF 0.092 ([results](benchmarks/tts/2026-08-19.md)) |
| [Tsukasa Speech](https://github.com/Respaired/Tsukasa-Speech) | Respair | dedicated | — | PyTorch | weights ~4.7 GB | CC-BY-NC-4.0 | no | Very fast (RTF 0.015), anime style; non-commercial; dependency fixes needed ([results](benchmarks/tts/2026-08-19.md)) |
| [mio-tts-cpp](https://github.com/mmnga/mio-tts-cpp) | mmnga | dedicated | — | C++ / GGML (no Python) | ~489 MB (0.1B Q8 + codec) | TBD | TBD | Best for CPU/embedded (RTF 0.179, ~550 MB RAM); normalize numbers beforehand ([results](benchmarks/tts/2026-08-19.md)) |
| [CosyVoice3 0.5B](https://github.com/FunAudioLLM/CosyVoice) | Alibaba (FunAudioLLM) | multilingual | yes | PyTorch, ONNX | 0.5B (full download ~9 GB) | Apache-2.0 | yes | Good quality (RTF 0.557); Japanese needs katakana preprocessing ([results](benchmarks/tts/2026-08-19.md)) |
| [Supertonic3](https://github.com/supertone-inc/supertonic) | Supertone | multilingual | — | ONNX (C++ / C# / Go / Rust / Node, etc.) | 99M | MIT | yes | Near real time on CPU, 31 languages; repository archived in 2026-07 ([results](benchmarks/tts/2026-08-19.md)) |
| [Qwen3-TTS 0.6B](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-TTS) | Alibaba (Qwen) | multilingual | yes | PyTorch | 0.6B | Apache-2.0 | yes | Strong voice instructions/design/cloning; slow without optimization (RTF 2.27) ([results](benchmarks/tts/2026-08-19.md)) |
| [Kokoro-82M](https://huggingface.co/hexgrad/Kokoro-82M) | hexgrad | multilingual | yes | PyTorch, ONNX | 82M | Apache-2.0 | yes | Japanese phonemization broke down (short-text CER 3.4); not usable for Japanese ([results](benchmarks/tts/2026-08-19.md)) |
| [Fish Audio S2 Pro](https://github.com/fishaudio/fish-speech) | Fish Audio | multilingual | yes | PyTorch | 4B (weights ~11 GB, VRAM 24 GB +) | Research License | no | Could not run on a 12 GB GPU; not measured |

## LLM

For Japanese knowledge and reasoning, see the existing leaderboards:

- [Nejumi LLM Leaderboard](https://wandb.ai/llm-leaderboard/nejumi-leaderboard4/reports/Nejumi-LLM-Leaderboaed-4--VmlldzoxNDQyMzkxMA)
- [Swallow LLM Leaderboard](https://swallow-llm.github.io/swallow-leaderboard-v2.en.html)

We measure what matters for dialogue — **time to first token and tokens per second** — on a local GPU ([benchmarks/llm/2026-11-lmstudio.md](benchmarks/llm/2026-11-lmstudio.md)).
